mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in WORKPLACES mobility from its current low base signals more commuting and lunch-trip demand, which lifts retail and recreation visits within four weeks. The effect should appear as WORKPLACES becomes less negative and RETAIL_REC moves up from roughly -78%.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -69.4 to -64.7 while TRANSIT stayed near -73 to -76
failure_condition: Reject if WORKPLACES continues to improve for two consecutive weekly means but RETAIL_REC does not rise versus the prior 4-week average within 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rebound in PARKS mobility indicates discretionary out-of-home activity and improving willingness to travel for nonessential trips; that spillover should translate into higher retail and recreation mobility over the next one to two weeks. This mechanism fails if the parks rebound is isolated and does not broaden to shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns positive after a negative week-on-week reading
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -27.7 to 5.7 and then back to -3.6
failure_condition: Reject if PARKS crosses from below zero to above zero but RETAIL_REC is not less negative over the following 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain deeply suppressed, retail and recreation will stay depressed because commuting-linked footfall and spontaneous center-city trips remain constrained. The next four weeks should therefore show no recovery or a further decline in RETAIL_REC unless mobility restrictions ease materially.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -70 and WORKPLACES remains below -60
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is about -73 and WORKPLACES about -65
failure_condition: Reject if TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay below the stated thresholds for two weeks but RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week mean within 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A further increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility implies more time spent at home and fewer out-of-home discretionary purchases, which should push RETAIL_REC lower over the next week. The effect should be immediate because the home-stay signal is already elevated near 27%.
failure_condition: Reject if RESIDENTIAL increases week-on-week but RETAIL_REC becomes less negative within the next 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM remains much less depressed than RETAIL_REC, households are still making only essential trips, not discretionary shopping trips. That pattern predicts flat or weaker retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks unless nonessential visit intensity catches up.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above -35 while RETAIL_REC stays below -75
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is around -29 to -35 while RETAIL_REC is around -77 to -80
failure_condition: Reject if the gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC remains at least 40 points for two weeks but RETAIL_REC rises toward baseline within 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT recovers by at least 5 points from its current level, retail and recreation should improve within two weeks because easier access to shopping and leisure districts increases trip completion rates. The signal fails if transit improves only for work trips while discretionary movement stays muted.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises at least 5 points from its current weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -76.4 to -73.0 while RETAIL_REC remained near -77 to -80
failure_condition: Reject if TRANSIT rises by 5 or more points and RETAIL_REC does not become less negative within 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained PARKS rebound combined with higher RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates warmer-weather, local-area substitution away from indoor venues, which should modestly lift retail and recreation over the next four weeks. The mechanism requires both outdoor activity and home-based neighborhood spending to move together.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both rise week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped to 5.7 in t-1w while RESIDENTIAL stayed elevated near 27
failure_condition: Reject if PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both rise for two weeks but RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the subsequent 28 days.
